Choose the 100-customer capped launch, with enrollment increased in stages and rollback available throughout. Its delayed revenue is a real cost, but the current evidence supports only latency performance for 20 customers in one region. It does not establish performance at broader scale, and weekly failure checks leave reliability uncertain.

Before increasing enrollment, add timely failure monitoring and define operational thresholds that pause enrollment or trigger rollback. Run load tests toward the intended cap and check performance after each enrollment increase. Keep the initial scope in the tested region; expansion to other regions needs its own checks.

Treat 100 customers as a ceiling, not a proven safe capacity. Expand beyond the cap only after larger-load results and observed failure impacts support that decision. With no failure-loss estimates, the revenue-versus-risk tradeoff cannot be quantified; the capped approach preserves a practical opportunity to learn and reverse course.
